For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether Energy in one place relates to Transport in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_energy_transport.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Get ordered list of boroughs from dataset
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
print('Number of boroughs:', n)

# Create index mapping
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = row['borough']
    b2 = row['neighbor']
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1  # Make symmetric

# Check row sums (number of neighbors)
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
print('Min neighbors:', row_sums.min())
print('Max neighbors:', row_sums.max())
print('Boroughs with 0 neighbors:', np.sum(row_sums == 0))

# Row-standardize W
W_row = np.zeros_like(W)
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        W_row[i, :] = W[i, :] / row_sums[i]
    else:
        W_row[i, i] = 1  # Isolated borough gets self-weight

# Get variables
x = df['Energy_value'].values
y = df['Transport_value'].values

# Center variables
x_c = x - x.mean()
y_c = y - y.mean()

# Compute Lee's L statistic
# L = (n / S0) * (x' W y) / sqrt((x'x)(y'y))
# For row-standardized W, S0 = n (sum of all weights = n)
S0 = W_row.sum()
print('S0:', S0)

# Spatial lag of y
Wy = W_row @ y_c

# Lee's L
numerator = x_c @ Wy
denominator = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_c @ y_c))
L_obs = (n / S0) * numerator / denominator

print('Observed Lee L:', L_obs)
print('Numerator (x_c @ Wy):', numerator)
print('Denominator:', denominator)

# Permutation test - shuffle y values across boroughs
np.random.seed(42)
n_permutations = 1000
L_perm = np.zeros(n_permutations)

for p in range(n_permutations):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y_c)
    Wy_perm = W_row @ y_perm
    num_perm = x_c @ Wy_perm
    den_perm = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_perm @ y_perm))
    L_perm[p] = (n / S0) * num_perm / den_perm

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm) >= np.abs(L_obs))
print('Permutation p-value (two-tailed):', p_value)
print('Mean of permuted L:', np.mean(L_perm))
print('Std of permuted L:', np.std(L_perm))
print('Min permuted L:', np.min(L_perm))
print('Max permuted L:', np.max(L_perm))
"} <|tool_call_end|> <|tool_calls_section_end|>

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_energy_transport.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    a = row['borough']
    b = row['neighbor']
    if a in idx and b in idx:
        i = idx[a]
        j = idx[b]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1

row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
Wr = np.zeros_like(W)
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        Wr[i] = W[i] / row_sums[i]
    else:
        Wr[i, i] = 1

x = df['Energy_value'].values
y = df['Transport_value'].values
xc = x - x.mean()
yc = y - y.mean()

S0 = Wr.sum()
num = xc @ (Wr @ yc)
den = np.sqrt((xc @ xc) * (yc @ yc))
L = (n / S0) * num / den

print('Observed Lee L:', L)

np.random.seed(42)
perms = 1000
Lp = np.zeros(perms)
for k in range(perms):
    yp = np.random.permutation(yc)
    nump = xc @ (Wr @ yp)
    denp = np.sqrt((xc @ xc) * (yp @ yp))
    Lp[k] = (n / S0) * nump / denp

pval = np.mean(np.abs(Lp) >= np.abs(L))
print('Two-tailed p-value:', pval)
print('Permutation mean:', np.mean(Lp))
print('Permutation std:', np.std(Lp))
print('95% CI for null:', np.percentile(Lp, [2.5, 97.5]))
```
